tone_statements.citation: Greve, Theis Kudsk. 2024. Number and possessive marking on Thuri nouns. Thesis or dissertation, The University of Edinburgh (School of Philosophy, Psychology and Language Sciences; related person: Bert Remijsen). Edinburgh Research Archive, hdl:1842/43202, doi:10.7488/era/5752 (issued 2024-07-12; available on ERA 2025-03-13; file).
tone_statements.quote: Thuri is a tonal language as is the norm in the Western Nilotic family. The items in this dataset display the tones: high, mid, low, fall and rise. However a full investigation specifically into the tonal system to determine underlying inventory and allophonic/allomorphic variation was not conducted for this dissertation, though it is clear that tonal changes are used in morphological marking in Thuri as will be expanded on in the relevant sections below.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2010. Morphosyntax of Luwo. In O. Hieda (ed.), Descriptive Studies of Nilotic Morphosyntax (Studies in Nilotic Linguistics 2), 1-27. Tokyo: ILCAA; and Storch, Anne. 2007. Grammatical change and emblematic features in Western Nilotic. ACAL 37 proceedings, 1-15.
sources.note: Thuri mentioned only in classification/contact remarks; Storch 2010 p. 26 lists Thuri among languages that 'still remain largely unexplored'. No Thuri stress statement.

sources.citation: Gilley, Leoma G. 2004. The Lwoian family. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 165-174. Entebbe: SIL-Sudan.
sources.note: Nothing for Thuri. p. 165: 'Thuri is very similar to Luwo, and for the most part, they are able to use the Luwo materials. They have not developed a separate writing system at this point.' Stress remarks in the volume concern Shilluk/Dinka/Nuer orthography only; back matter (contents of OPSL 1-8) lists no Thuri paper.

sources.citation: Storch, Anne. 2003. Dynamics of interacting populations: language contact in the Lwoo languages of Bahr el-Ghazal. Studies in African Linguistics 32(1): 65-93.
sources.note: Thuri number-marking data and a note on its two mutually exclusive ATR vowel sets; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Record and project blurb only: a first descriptive report on Thuri that 'covers key features of phonology, morphology, and syntax' (web-search summary of the Edinburgh pages). Given the author (West Nilotic tone/quantity specialist) and the student thesis it fed (work 1, which calls Thuri tonal with H/M/L/Fall/Rise), it very likely presents the tone and vowel-length inventory, but no tone wording was seen.
